name: Birth Certificate
department: Office of the Registrar General of India — Civil Registration System (CRS)
summary: Official proof of birth registered with the local municipal or panchayat authority, issued under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
eligibility: Every birth occurring in India must be registered within 21 days, free of charge, by the parent/guardian or the hospital
Late registration (after 21 days) is possible with a late fee and, beyond 1 year, may require a magistrate's order
documents: Hospital-issued birth intimation slip, or affidavit for home births
Proof of parents' identity and address (Aadhaar, etc.)
Proof of date and place of birth
fee: Free within 21 days of birth. Late registration fees and certified copy charges vary by state/municipality, typically ₹5-100 depending on delay.
process: Hospital or informant reports the birth to the local registrar (municipal corporation/panchayat)
Registration is entered into the state's Civil Registration System (CRS)
Apply for the certificate online via your state's e-District/CRS portal or in person at the municipal office
Pay applicable fee (free if within 21 days) and download or collect the certificate
source: Office of the Registrar General of India (CRS)

faq.question: What if the birth wasn't registered within 21 days?
faq.answer: It can still be registered late with a delay fee and, in some states, a self-declaration or affidavit. Registrations delayed beyond one year generally require an order from a magistrate/executive authority designated by the state.

faq.question: Where do I actually apply — is this a central portal?
faq.answer: Registration and certificate issuance happen at the state/municipal level. crsorgi.gov.in is the central framework; the actual application goes through your state's CRS or e-District portal, which inLens links to on the state-specific version of this page.
